alignments.note: κρατέω → holding fast; the adverbial particle is part of the verb's own English expression, headed on the verb word.
Present passive participle with its copular auxiliary as a rule 9 helper.
συμβιβαζόμενον → knit together; together realizes the συν- preverb and rides inside the verb's unit (rule 106), headed on the verb word.

αὔξει → increaseth with. τὴν αὔξησιν is accusative, and rule 21 hands a governed word only the preposition that realizes its own case; an accusative has none, so the supplied with is the verb's own government and stays inside its unit. That is rule 106's accusative arm in terms: a preposition standing over an accusative object is the verb's or the frame's and never the object's. Head on the lexical verb under rule 17. The competing reading, with the riding on the article under rule 21, is what the accusative forecloses, and this chapter already keeps such a preposition with the verb at COL.2.8 (maketh spoil of / bare you) and COL.2.15 (triumphing over / bare them).
Article → the. The article takes the English determiner the ASV wrote for it and nothing more, the preposition having stayed with the verb under rule 106's accusative arm.
αὔξησιν → increase, the accusative standing on its bare noun.
Rule 23: article before a name with no English determiner.
Determinerless genitive: of God is one unit on the noun under rule 21.

review_notes: Corrected s019/s020: the accepted alignment gave with the to the article as an 'accusative-of-manner's English preposition', but rules 21 and 106 both deny an accusative a case preposition — rule 21 says in terms that an English preposition licensed by something else does not move to a word merely because it stands in front of it, and rule 106's accusative arm says such a preposition is the verb's or the frame's and never the object's. with now rides inside αὔξει's unit headed on increaseth, and τήν keeps the bare the the ASV wrote for it.

This also brings the verse into line with the rest of the chapter, which already keeps a preposition standing over an accusative inside the verb: maketh spoil of at COL.2.8, triumphing over at COL.2.15, and dwelling in at COL.2.18. That is rule 24's habit applied to one construction.
The remaining 21 units are unchanged and were re-verified; the partition still covers all 23 source and all 27 target ids exactly once.
s003 holding fast heads on holding and s018 knit together on knit — rule 106's rule that the head is the word glossing the verbal root and never the particle.
